Series::dsplit¶

Back to Series API Reference

Signatures¶

Series::dsplit(std::int64_t sections) const -> std::vector<Series>
Series::dsplit(pluss::RangeView::Int indices) const -> std::vector<Series>

What It Does¶

dsplit() is tensor_split() pinned to the depth axis — axis 2. It requires a Series of rank >= 3. Otherwise it matches hsplit() and vsplit(): dsplit(sections) needs axis 2 to be exactly divisible by sections and returns sections equal slabs; dsplit(indices) cuts at the given depth boundaries. Each piece is a view.

Parameters¶

sections (std::int64_t)

Number of equal slabs; axis 2 length must be a multiple of it.

indices (pluss::RangeView::Int)

Depth boundary positions; n of them give n + 1 pieces.

Returns¶

std::vector<Series> Depth-slab views.

Gradient¶

Differentiable, exactly as hsplit().

Example¶

std::vector<double> d(2 * 2 * 4);
for (int i = 0; i < 16; ++i) d[i] = i;
auto cube = pluss::make_series(d, {2, 2, 4});

auto parts = cube.dsplit(2);
std::cout << "pieces=" << parts.size()
          << "  each shape [" << parts[0].sizes()[0] << ","
          << parts[0].sizes()[1] << "," << parts[0].sizes()[2] << "]";

Output¶

pieces=2  each shape [2,2,2]

Gotchas And Failure Modes¶

  • Requires rank >= 3; lower-rank input raises.

  • The integer form demands exact divisibility of axis 2.

  • Pieces are views over the source storage.

Summary¶

dsplit() splits axis 2 (depth) of a rank->= 3 Series:

  • dsplit(n) — n equal slabs, exact divisibility required

  • dsplit(indices) — cut at depth boundaries

  • zero-copy views; differentiable

See Also¶

  • Series::hsplit / Series::vsplit: the horizontal and vertical counterparts.

  • Series::tensor_split: the general form on any axis.
